title: Colony and Archive
premise: Silas Dravenmoor, the seventh clone of a murdered colonial founder, keeps the beacon on the dead world of Kestrel's Landing that no record says was ever built. When a name appears on a ship's manifest for a vessel that never launched, Silas discovers the beacon is an archive of suppressed memories — including the original's own, and proof of who ordered his death. The message inside could end the decades-long war between the colonies and Earth's Directorate, but delivering it means exposing Silas himself as evidence. In the end, Silas broadcasts the archive and chooses to let their cloned identity dissolve into the collective memory they freed, ending the war by refusing to be anyone's property.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned colonial settlement records before turning to fiction. They write about memory as both inheritance and weapon from a farmhouse full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Silas Dravenmoor performs the daily maintenance ritual on the Kestrel's Landing beacon, narrating their solitary routine and the gaps in official records surrounding it. A routine diagnostic returns an anomaly: a manifest entry for the freighter Halcyon Vow, a ship registry says was never constructed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath practiced order.

chapters.title: Seventh of His Name
chapters.summary: Silas travels to the colony capital to renew their identity license and confronts the Archivist-General, who reveals Silas is the seventh clone of founder Elias Dravenmoor — and that clones one through five all died violently. The sixth vanished. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under a carefully maintained sense of self.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Back at the beacon, Silas decrypts the Halcyon Vow entry and finds a passenger list of people history says never existed, including a woman named Ione Vashti whose face triggers fragmented memories that are not Silas's own. The beacon begins transmitting unprompted. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Sixth Left Behind
chapters.summary: A stranger arrives at the beacon: Wren, claiming to be the sixth clone, half-mad from carrying partial memories of the original's murder. Wren warns that the Directorate has been hunting the archive for thirty years and that Silas's renewal filing flagged them. POV: alternating Silas and Wren. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two broken copies.

chapters.title: The Archive in the Antenna
chapters.summary: Together they breach the beacon's core and find it is not a transmitter but a vault: the original's full memories, digitized, including his discovery that the Directorate engineered the colony war to justify consolidation. The murder was the first casualty of the cover-up. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Ice Plain
chapters.summary: Directorate retrieval teams land, forcing Silas and Wren across the frozen wastes with the archive key. Wren is captured buying time; Silas hears them screaming their real name — Elias's name — as they're taken. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve, and survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: Ione Vashti, Alive
chapters.summary: Silas reaches the Halcyon Vow's hidden dry dock and finds Ione Vashti alive, aged, hiding aboard the never-flown ship — the original's lover and the only witness to his murder. She reveals the message: a peace framework the original died carrying, which both sides still fear. POV: Ione. Emotional beat: two keepers of the dead finding common cause.

chapters.title: The Price of the Message
chapters.summary: To broadcast the archive, someone must merge with it manually — becoming the message, their individual identity overwritten. Ione is too old to survive the interface. Silas realizes why they were cloned: every Dravenmoor copy is a compatible vessel, bred as a delivery mechanism. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror at being designed, then acceptance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Under fire from Directorate ships, Silas interfaces with the beacon and lets Elias's memories flood through them, broadcasting the murder, the manufactured war, and the peace terms to every colony and Earth simultaneously. Wren's capture footage goes out with it. The Directorate fleet stands down as its crews mutiny. POV: Silas, dissolving. Emotional beat: climax — self-annihilation as liberation.

chapters.title: Colony and Archive
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the war over, colonists tend the beacon as a memorial. Ione teaches children the names from the impossible manifest. A young archivist finds a new entry appearing: a voice, neither Elias nor Silas, signing itself 'the seventh,' still keeping watch. POV: Ione. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — memory outlives identity, and that is enough.
